tips: Pre-load Suica into your Apple/Google Wallet while at MSP to bypass ticket machines on arrival.
Set your phone timezone to JST mid-flight and take melatonin around 13:00 CT to align your clock.
Hit the Limousine Bus counter at Haneda before baggage claim to secure spots for all 8.
If Ichiran line is apocalyptic, pivot one stop north to Shin-Okubo Koreatown for KFC and cheese dogs.

2026-12-16.weatherAlert: December in Tokyo is typically dry, but occasional cold rain is possible. The Shibuya Blue Cave illumination and Meiji Shrine walk are fully exposed.

suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Miyashita Park covered rooftop + Parco + Tower Records (9 floors) absorb a full wet afternoon without surfacing.
suggestedSwap.reason: If it rains, the outdoor 600k LED walk will be miserable; the covered Miyashita Park/Parco complex keeps the squad dry and entertained.

tips: Shibuya Sky sunset slots sell out fast; book the exact 16:00 slot online weeks in advance for your group of 8.
If day one cooked the crew, swap Blue Cave for an early nomihodai and 23:00 lights-out.

2026-12-17.weatherAlert: Nakamise street and Hoppy Street are outdoor and offer little shelter from sudden cold rain.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Ueno Ameyoko market under the tracks
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Tokyo National Museum (samurai swords + armor, 2h) slots between Asakusa and Akiba on the same line.
suggestedSwap.reason: If rain hits, the open-air Ueno market is a cold, wet slog; the nearby National Museum is indoor, world-class, and perfectly situated.

tips: Arrive at Senso-ji by 08:30 to get photos before the 10:00 tour bus crush.
If Skytree queue is insane, pivot to Asahi Beer Hall's 22F Sky Room next door for the same river view with a beer in hand.
teamLab Planets requires bare feet; wear easy-slip shoes and avoid complicated boots.
Ginza depachika (basement food hall) raids are best at 15:00 when bento boxes start getting discounted for the evening.

2026-12-19.weatherAlert: High rain risk for a coastal day trip. The Enoden coastal tram views and Enoshima island climb are weather-dependent.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Enoshima island — climb to the Sea Candle
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Enoshima onsen finish: Enospa overlooks the bay — soak with a Fuji view before the train if legs are cooked.
suggestedSwap.reason: If rain hits, the Sea Candle climb is slippery and views are obscured; Enospa onsen provides a warm, weather-proof bay view.

tips: Wakakusa-yama in Nara closes the second Sunday of December—don't let anyone convince you to add it to tomorrow's itinerary!
Grab a hot corn soup from a vending machine on the Fushimi Inari descent tomorrow morning—it's a December lifesaver.
Run the Airbnb washer during dinner so everyone lands in Kyoto with a clean kit.
If Golden Gai peaked on the 18th, pivot to Shinjuku Batting Center for $3 (¥500) of midnight swings.

2026-12-21.weatherAlert: Gion golden hour and Kamo River bank are exposed to cold December winds; clear nights drop close to freezing.
tips: Book Pontocho Alley riverside izakaya well in advance; 8-person tables on the river are rare.
L'Escamoteur steampunk bar opens at 20:00—send two scouts at 19:40 to hold the queue between dinner and the alley crawl.

2026-12-22.weatherAlert: Fushimi Inari at dawn is cold, often near freezing in late December. Dress in layers.
tips: Past Yotsutsuji the crowds hit zero—the full summit loop (+45 min) buys a deserted mountain and bragging rights.
Sake Bar Yoramu has only 8 seats—perfect for half the squad to surrender to the bartender's 'osusume' recommendations.

2026-12-23.weatherAlert: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove offers zero shelter; rain turns the path into a crowded, umbrella-clashing gauntlet.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove before the buses exist
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Sanjusangendo — 1,001 golden Kannon statues in a 120m hall. Indoor, jaw-dropping, criminally underrated.
suggestedSwap.reason: If it rains, the bamboo grove is a miserable, crowded umbrella-war; Sanjusangendo is an indoor, awe-inspiring alternative nearby.

tips: Wakakusa-yama is closed for the winter—do not attempt the hike today.
When feeding deer, bow first, show empty hands when done, and never run—they read it as a game they will win.

2026-12-24.crowdAlert: KFC for Christmas dinner is a massive Japanese tradition; pre-ordering is often required, or expect 2+ hour lines.
tips: If all 8 lost the Nintendo Museum lottery, pivot to Byodo-in and Tsuen tea in Uji for a matcha-heavy morning.
Buy a jiggly Rikuro's cheesecake near Namba station for the house—it will not survive the night.

2026-12-25.crowdAlert: USJ Christmas Day is peak capacity; Super Nintendo World timed entry will be a bloodbath without Express Passes.
tips: Rope-drop the gates 45 min early and sprint to SNW immediately to beat the timed-entry rush.
If Kinopio's Cafe is full, Yoshi's snack stand + popcorn buckets + Power-Up Band challenges still deliver the serotonin.

2026-12-26.weatherAlert: Miyajima island and the floating torii are highly exposed to coastal winds and rain; the ferry ride can be brutally cold.
tips: This is the longest day of the trip—anyone redlining should skip Miyajima, do the museum unhurried, and meet at Hiroshima station.
If the museum hits heavy (it will), Shukkei-en garden 10 min from the station offers a quiet, contemplative Edo walk.

2026-12-27.weatherAlert: The Midosuji Illumination is a 4km outdoor walk; cold December winds can make this exhausting if not dressed properly.
tips: Buy 551 Horai butaman 4-pack from Namba station BEFORE the crab dinner—they sell out nightly and house breakfast depends on it.
If Ura-Namba was Wednesday's love story, the JR Tenma standing-bar belt is tonight's sequel—izakaya density world record.
Kobe beef budget fork: $22 (¥3,500) bowls and croquette stands around Sannomiya deliver 70% of the experience at 40% of the price.
Do a tax-free paperwork check tonight: receipts with passports, purchases accessible—customs CAN ask on exit.
Sit on the LEFT side of the Nozomi eastbound for Fuji's encore.
Zero-out your Suica card at the konbini and hit the final boss gachapon at the gate before boarding.

globalTips: With the USD/JPY rate at ~161.68, your dollar stretches far—avoid exchanging cash at airports and simply withdraw from 7-Eleven ATMs for the best rates.
December evenings in Tokyo, Kyoto, and Osaka drop close to freezing with biting wind chill; pack a warm, wind-resistant outer layer rather than bulky sweaters.
For a group of 8, always split into two squads of 4 for restaurants, bars, and karaoke—Japanese venues rarely seat octets without prior reservation.
